title: Preterm and newborn size charts (INTERGROWTH-21st) and growth velocity
_comment: Tables give the measurement at each whole z-score (columns z_minus3..z_plus3) per gestational age (ga_wk + ga_d, weeks+days) or per postmenstrual age (pma_wk, exact weeks). Engine: find the row for the age, then linearly interpolate the measured value between the bracketing z columns to get z; beyond the outer columns report as below/above the outer column. Centile = standard normal CDF of z. Weight in kg, length and head circumference in cm.

method.text: Each table row lists the measurement at z scores -3, -2, -1, 0, +1, +2, +3 (column headers in the source). The engine interpolates z between adjacent columns; the z_0 column is the median. This is a reading of published tables, not a published equation: INTERGROWTH-21st GAMLSS equations are in the Lancet papers, which could not be fetched (thelancet.com and sciencedirect returned HTTP 403).

charts.name: INTERGROWTH-21st Very Preterm Size at Birth Reference

note.quote: The International Very Preterm Size at Birth Reference Charts
Data derived from cross-sectional measurements at birth should not be used to monitor postnatal growth (they cannot provide “growth” patterns).

charts.name: INTERGROWTH-21st Postnatal Growth Standards for Preterm Infants

note.quote: Weight, length, and head circumference for preterm infants until they reached 64 weeks’ postmenstrual age.

exponential.vars: W = weight in grams, D = day, 1 = beginning of interval, n = end of interval
exponential.quote: Exponential model (EM) 18 : estimated GV = [ 1000 × ln ( W n W 1 ) ] ( D n − D 1 ) .

definitions.quote: where W=weight in grams, D= day, 1=beginning of time interval and n=end of time interval in days.

target.text: example desirable rate cited by the authors, not a guideline
target.quote: This provides an objective measure of the infant’s growth which we can compare to a desirable growth rate, such as 18g/kg/day
